Would that this day I had le[ft] the ball in the carpenter's house —
2	[the carpenter's wife, who is like the moth]er who bore me — would that I had le[ft it there;]
3	the ca[rpenter's daughter, who is like my] little [si]ster — would th[at I had left it there!]
4	Today my ba[ll] fe[ll] down into the earth;
5	my mallet f[ell down] into the earth.
Enkidu ans[wered(?)] Gilgameš:
Gilgameš [answered(?)] Enkidu:
[Enkidu] went down [to the earth,]
but he did not hold [to the instruction of Gilgame]š:
he put on a c[lean garment,]
and they knew him for the str[anger] he was;
he anointed himself with sw[eet] oil from the flask,
and at [its] scent they gathered about him;
he slung a throw-stick i[n the earth,]
and the shades were trembling;
those [struck] by the throw-stick ringed him round;
he l[if]ted a cudgel in [his] hand,
and [the shades] were trembling;
[he put] shoes o[n his feet;]
[he raised] a cry [in the earth;]
[he kissed] the wif[e he loved;]
[he struck the w]if[e he] hated;
he ki[ssed the s]o[n] he loved;
he str[uck the so]n he hated —
and the out[cr]y of the earth seized him:
Then [E]nkidu [would rise] from the earth to the up[per world:]
Namt[ar did not sei]ze him; the Demon did not seize him; the ear[th seiz]ed him;
the merciless amb[usher Nergal] did not seize him; the eart[h seize]d him;
he did not fall on the field of the b[attle of m]ales; the earth seized him.
Then [the ki]ng, the son of Ninsun, wept for his servant Enkidu:
to Ekur, the house of Enlil, he went all alone:
Father Enlil answered him not a word.
[To Ur, the house of Sîn,] he went [all alone:]
Fa[ther Sîn answered him not a word.]
T[o Eridu, the house of Ea, he went all alone:]

F[ather Ea — today my ball fell down into the earth,]
74	[my] mal[let fell down into the earth,]
75	and Enkid[u, who went down to bring them up — the earth seized him!]
76	Namtar did n[ot seize him; the Demon did not seize him; the earth seized him;]
77	the mercil[ess] ambusher Nergal [did not seize him; the earth seized him;]
78	[he did not fall on] the field of the battle of ma[les; the earth seized him!]
Father Ea, i[n ... ,]
[spoke] to the fighter, the yo[ung man Šamaš:]

Fighter, young man, Šam[aš, son of Ningal ... —]
82	now, [open a chink into the earth;]
83	[bring up] the phantom of En[kidu from the earth like a breath of wind,]
84	at the wo[rd of ... !]
The fighter, the young man Šamaš, son of Nin[gal ... ,]
opened a chink into the earth,
and brought up the phantom of Enkidu from the earth like a breath of wind.
They embraced each other and kept kissing;
they traded counsel, asking, asking:

Tell me, my friend — tell me, my friend!
91	Tell me the order of the earth that you saw!

I will not tell you, my friend; I will not tell you.
93	If I tell you the order of the earth that I saw —
94	[yo]u — sit down and weep!
Then [I] will sit down and weep.

[My friend — the pe]nis you handled, and your heart was glad:
97	[ ... like an] old [be]am the worm devours it;
98	[my friend — the crotch you] handled, and your heart was glad:
99	[like a crack in the ear]th it is full of dust.
[Woe! he] cried, [and threw] himself [in the dust;]
["Woe!"] cried [Gilgameš,] and threw himself [in the du]st.
[The one with one son — did you s]ee him? "I saw:
[a peg is se]t [in his wall,] and [bitterly] he weeps over it."
[The one with two sons — did you see him? "I s]aw:
[he sits on two bricks,] eating bread."
[The one with three sons — did you see him?] "I saw:
[from the waterskin slung at the saddle] he drinks water."
[The one with four sons — did you se]e him? "I saw:
[like the owner of a te]am [of donkeys] his heart is glad."
[The one with five sons — did] you [s]ee him? "I saw:
[like a] fine [scrib]e, his hand kept open,
[straight] into the palace he enters."
[The one with six sons — did] you [s]ee him? "I saw:
[like a ploughman his heart is glad."]
[The one with seven sons — did you see him? "I saw:]
[as a junior among the gods he sits on a throne, hearing the proceedings(?)."]
[The one with no heir — did you see him? "I saw:]
like a fine banner(?) he is pinne[d] in a co[rn]er."
Like [ ... ]
[The one who ... — did you see him? "I saw:]
[The one who ... — did you see him? "I saw:]
The one struck by a mooring-pole — did you see him? "I [saw:]
alas for his mother [and] his f[ath]er! — whenever pegs are pulled, he [wa]nders witho[ut rest."]
The one who [died] the death of [his] god — did you [s]ee him? "I sa[w:]
he sleeps in the bed of [the god]s, drinking clear water."
The one killed in battle — did you see him? "I s[aw:]
his father and mother cradle his head, and his wife [weep]s [over] him."
The one whose corpse lies thro[wn] on the open land — did you see him? "I saw:
his shade finds no sleep in the earth."
The one whose shade has no one to tend it — did you see him? "I saw:
scrapings of the pot and crusts of bread thrown in the street — that is what he eats."
